# Git Internals & Enterprise Version Control

::: {.callout-note}
**Part 11: DevOps Engineering, IaC & Observability** · Section 11.1  
*Ubuntu 26.04 LTS ("Resolute Raccoon") Reference Platform*
:::

## Executive Summary & Objectives

This chapter establishes the engineering foundations, operational mental models, and production workflows for **Git Internals & Enterprise Version Control** within modern Ubuntu 26.04 LTS environments.

## Syllabus & Focus Areas

- [ ] **Git Plumbing & Object Model:** Blobs, trees, commits, annotated tags, content-addressable `.git/objects`, packfiles, reflog recovery (`git reflog`, `git fsck`)
- [ ] **Advanced Workflows:** Trunk-based development vs GitFlow, interactive rebase (`git rebase -i`, `autosquash`), `git bisect` automated bug hunting, `git worktree`, submodules vs subtrees
- [ ] **Cryptographic Commit Signing:** Signing commits and tags with SSH keys (OpenSSH `allowed_signers`) or GPG keys, enforcing verified signatures in branch protection rules
- [ ] **Self-Hosted Git Platforms:** Deploying and operating Forgejo / Gitea and GitLab CE on Ubuntu 26.04 (PostgreSQL tuning, Redis/Valkey, Gitaly, object storage backends)

## Architectural Concepts & Mental Model

Understanding the subsystem architecture, system boundary layers, and kernel-userspace interactions:

- **Target Release Context:** Standardized on Ubuntu 26.04 LTS defaults (Linux 7.0 generic kernel, pure `cgroup v2`, `sudo-rs`, OpenSSH 10.2).
- **Core Abstractions:** Subsystem primitives, state machines, and configuration hierarchies.
- **Integration Points:** Interaction with `systemd`, security layers (AppArmor 4.x), and network/storage fabrics.

## Safe Inspection & Diagnostics

Execute safe, non-destructive inspection commands to inspect operational state:

```bash
# Verify active subsystem state and version baseline
uname -r
uptime
```

## Production Implementation & Patterns

Key configuration patterns, standard file paths, and declarative declarations:

- Primary configuration files and directories.
- Canonical implementation patterns for production deployments.
- Operational maintenance and change validation procedures.

## Common Traps, Failure Modes & Recovery

| Symptom / Failure Mode | Root Cause | Safe Remediation & Recovery |
|------------------------|------------|-----------------------------|
| Service startup failure / degraded state | Configuration syntax or permission mismatch | Inspect unit status and journal logs (`journalctl -xeu <unit>`) |
| Unintended state mutation | Legacy utility flag discrepancies | Verify command semantics against `rust-coreutils` and `sudo-rs` |
| Latency or resource starvation | Unbounded resource exhaustion | Check cgroup pressure metrics (`/proc/pressure/*`) |

## Verification & Documentation Checklist
